seal.statement: During preparation and execution the comparative campaign never obtains an image, a harness commit or a reference-client package from the network on its own initiative and never substitutes another source or outcome when one is missing: an absent image is a typed image_unavailable refusal naming host, role and image, with --pull=never on every campaign docker run; an absent harness commit is a typed load_generator_commit_absent refusal before any worktree exists; the reference client installs offline only and a missing tarball is a typed offline_cache_incomplete refusal naming it; a host whose thermal decision cannot be read stays excluded and the exclusion carries a typed reason. Placement of images, the harness commit and the reference-client cache is an explicit provisioning step that exists in code for every supported target (the home lab and GCP), so no target that worked before is left with only a refusal.

ALTITUDE CHECK after the fifth rejection (2026-11-14, by the lead). Rejections one to four each found one unwitnessed or missing refusal; the fourth round answered with a census of the guards this change introduced. The fifth rejection shows the census had the wrong subject: it listed the guards the change added, not the decisions the provisioning script takes. docs/benchmarks/cloud/provision-gcp.sh is a short script whose every line either names something the operator chose, applies a default, probes and adapts, or tolerates a failure; three of its silent choices have now been found one at a time (the image family, the SSH key, the teardown result) and the verifier lists more (network, firewall reuse, package versions). Reassessment: the unit of the census is the script, line by line, not the diff. Decision recorded as CLASS REPAIR below.

CLASS REPAIR (2026-11-14, by the lead) for the root 'the GCP provisioning script silently chooses, adapts or tolerates'. CP-1 CENSUS OF THE SCRIPT. Every line of docs/benchmarks/cloud/provision-gcp.sh and of everything it invokes on the hosts (the startup script, the placement step) is classified as exactly one of: (a) a value the operator named; (b) a documented default, printed before anything is created; (c) a probe whose answer changes what the script does; (d) a failure that is tolerated ('|| true', '2>/dev/null' with no check, an unchecked exit status, a conditional that skips); (e) plain mechanics. The census is a table in the attempt record: line, class, what is decided, and its witness. CP-2 RULE. Class (c) and class (d) do not survive: a probe that adapts becomes either a named value or a refusal with usage before any gcloud call; a tolerated failure becomes a typed failure with a non-zero exit, except where the census shows the failure is the expected outcome of an idempotent step (for example deleting something that is already absent), in which case the script distinguishes 'absent' from 'failed' by asking, not by ignoring the exit status. Class (b) defaults are few, stated once in the script header and the guide, and printed with the values in use before the first create. CP-3 THE TWO FINDINGS. B6: the SSH public key file is named by the operator (one variable, following the script's convention); absent or unreadable is a usage refusal before any gcloud call; the script never searches for a key and never creates VMs without the ssh-keys metadata. B7: teardown reports what it deleted, what was already absent and what failed; any failure is a non-zero exit and the message names the resources that may still be billed; 'Teardown complete' is printed only after the script has asked and seen that no instance of the campaign remains. CP-4 NETWORK AND FIREWALL. The network is named or is the documented default, printed; an existing firewall rule with the script's name is used only if its rules are what the script would create (asked and compared), otherwise the script refuses and says what differs. CP-5 VERSIONS AND PROVENANCE. What the script installs or pulls without a pinned version (docker.io and git from the distribution archive, any image tag) is listed in the census; this quest does not pin them, but the provisioning record states for every host the VM image family and project, and the placement step records the installed versions and resolved image digests it observes, so that a campaign's evidence says what ran. If no provisioning record exists to carry them, the smallest one is added to the existing --provision output. CP-6 WITNESSES. Every class (b), former (c) and former (d) row has a witness executed against the gcloud stand-in through the script itself; mutants by row on the lab. CP-7 THE REPOSITORY HOLDS ITS OWN EVIDENCE. The runtime-owned non-empty storage directory case gets a witness inside the repository through the production deployer, and the generator of the real-ownership lab job is committed where the job's record can point to it. ROUTED, not repaired here: docs/benchmarks/cloud/provision-aws.sh and provision-azure.sh carry the same class (for example 'usermod -aG docker ubuntu || true') and are not on the campaign's path; a follow-up unit either gives them the same census or removes them.
